Actually that brings up an interesting idea.

Should up/down votes be public? I think there's a big argument against it since it could be used to start creating invasively accurate profiles of people. For instance SnoopSnoo is able to generate information about a reddit user just based on their posts. Even if it is little more than a collection of what you've voluntarily revealed it's kind of strange to see it all aggregated in one place. Now imagine if you could start factoring in things that somebody votes on. It'd be a dataminer, or harasser's, wet dream.

But I don't think that's the end of the question. What could be done is to show all posts somebody who has voted on, and how they voted, but without showing who the user is. So you could see for instance if 90% of somebody's posts are spent voting posts various politically correct subs and 10% are spent exclusively downvoting content in a variety of non politically correct subs that they don't otherwise participate in then it's be likely that they're a brigader. If you see a huge chunk of comments in a particular thread coming from these sorts then it's clear evidence that the thread is being brigaded.

Aside from preventing, or at least openly revealing brigading, it'd also be kind of fun as a poster to see what people who agree/disagree with what you're saying also happen to agree/disagree with.

edit It could lead to a new sort of amusing false flag attack. You start an account and start upvoting everything you can find in all sorts of the most repulsive subs you can find. Then you start upvoting stuff in a sub you disagree with to try to create a false association. Upvote brigading with stuff you disagree with. Screw it, I love the irony enough to make me like this idea even more.
